title: The bar is met, and the default deliberately stays 'ts'
description: With every divergence closed, the bar as originally written — equivalent: true — becomes satisfiable. Assert it directly, record that it is met, and say what a flip would now involve. This spec does not flip it.

successCriteria.description: The conformance harness reports equivalent: true on a real run of both engines, verified by running it.
The divergence-set pin becomes an equivalence assertion that still fails in BOTH directions — a new divergence fails it, and so does a silently-relaxed comparison.
docs/pge-graph.md's disposition is rewritten: which divergences closed and how, that the bar is met, and that the default stays 'ts' by choice rather than by blocker.
oracle-retention.test.ts still passes unmodified — pipeline.engine still defaults to 'ts', TsPipelineEngine is still selected and still the fallback.
Any field that did NOT converge is stated plainly with its reason, rather than the record implying total closure.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green, and the golden gate passing at or above its replay floor.

nonGoals: Claiming closure for a field that did not converge.
stopConditions: equivalent: true is not reached — record exactly which field still diverges and why, and do not adjust the comparison to reach it. A spec that closed three of four honestly is worth more than one that claims four.
definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green, the golden gate passing, and every documentation claim added backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
generatorNotes: This is the closing record; write it like one. The previous spec's closing section in docs/pge-graph.md is the model — it stated the outcome, named what was enforced by which test, and said what stayed unproven. The most valuable sentence here is the one that says what a flip would now actually require, now that the bar is no longer the blocker. Run the suite as `npx vitest run --exclude '**/.claude/worktrees/**' --exclude '**/node_modules/**'` — a bare run picks up nested worktrees. Verify on a CLEAN checkout, not just the working tree: this repo has twice been green locally and red in CI because uncommitted state was carrying the result.
evaluatorNotes: Verify equivalence by running the harness, not by reading the pin. Then mutation-test the new assertion in both directions. Finally read the prose against reality: every field it claims closed should be absent from a run you perform yourself. Run the suite as `npx vitest run --exclude '**/.claude/worktrees/**' --exclude '**/node_modules/**'` — a bare run picks up nested worktrees. Verify on a CLEAN checkout, not just the working tree: this repo has twice been green locally and red in CI because uncommitted state was carrying the result.

pendingAmendment.problem: sc-11-1 requires the conformance harness to report equivalent:true on a real run. That is now UNSATISFIABLE BY BUILDING: both remaining divergences are architectural, not unbuilt. `audits` was PROVEN unreachable in sprint 3 (the runtime cannot express a per-branch interrupt). `pipelineResult.errors` was proven unreachable in sprint 6 (only PgeEngine.run writes it, sourced from a checkpoint-gated commit refusal; the imperative commitAll is unconditional and ungated). They share ONE root cause.
pendingAmendment.resolution: Amend at sprint 11, preserving rigor rather than lowering the bar: replace 'the harness reports equivalent:true' with 'the harness reports the TRUE divergence set, and EVERY remaining entry is proven architectural rather than merely unbuilt, with a formal ADR-backed acceptance'. That is the same standard sprint 3 applied to `audits`. Do NOT weaken it to whatever the code happens to produce.
pendingAmendment.alsoOpen: Generator, evaluator and documenter all independently recommend joining pipelineResult.errors to the audits acceptance in .bober/architecture/arch-20260814-pge-full-convergence-adr-1.md. That ADR decision is UNTAKEN — it needs an architect, not a documenter. sc-11-3/sc-11-5 (rewrite the disposition, state plainly what did not converge) remain meetable as written.

amendment.amendedBy: orchestrator, on evaluator-adjudicated findings from sprints 3, 6, 8, 9

sc-11-1.literalForm: The conformance harness reports equivalent: true on a real run of both engines.
sc-11-1.status: UNSATISFIABLE BY BUILDING — not by shortfall.
sc-11-1.why: Two divergences remain and BOTH are architectural, sharing one root cause: the graph has a checkpoint-gated commit the imperative engine lacks. `audits` was PROVEN unreachable in sprint 3 (the runtime cannot express a per-branch interrupt). `pipelineResult.errors` was proven in sprint 6 (only PgeEngine.run writes it, from the interpreter's TaskFailure records; the imperative commitAll is unconditional and ungated, so there is no honest equivalent write site).
sc-11-1.amendedTo: The harness reports the TRUE divergence set on a real run of both engines, AND every remaining entry is proven architectural rather than merely unbuilt, each with a recorded reason. This preserves the bar's rigor instead of lowering it — it is the same standard sprint 3 applied to `audits`. It must NOT be met by adjusting the comparison.
sc-11-1.contractAlreadyAnticipatesThis: sc-11-5 requires any non-converged field be stated plainly, and the stopCondition says outright: 'A spec that closed three of four honestly is worth more than one that claims four.' The amendment aligns sc-11-1 with what the contract's own stopCondition and nonGoals already demand.

sc-11-2.amendedTo: The pin becomes an assertion of the TRUE state that still fails in BOTH directions — a NEW divergence fails it, AND a silently-relaxed comparison fails it. Unchanged in spirit; only the asserted state differs from 'empty'.

amendment.openRiskSprint11MustNotInherit: Sprint 10 measured NO channel breach on the real 29,214-byte workload — but its collaborators are STUBS. The `evaluations` channel measured 368/4096 with stub text (generator.notes='generated <id>', evaluator.summary='all criteria met'). This does NOT clear a real evaluator's longer free text against a cap sized to a ~1 KB stub corpus. Sprint 10's evaluator was explicit that this evidence CANNOT carry that claim. Do not let the closing record imply it does.
